findings.body: React will emit a missing-key warning and may misidentify/re-mount list items on reordering or filtering, causing incorrect component state reuse (e.g. stale action menu state) across re-renders of the filtered rule list.
findings.failure_mode: React list reconciliation degrades to index-based diffing for this branch, causing UI/console warnings and potential state bleed between list items.
findings.impact: React will emit a missing-key warning and may misidentify/re-mount list items on reordering or filtering, causing incorrect component state reuse (e.g. stale action menu state) across re-renders of the filtered rule list.
findings.root_cause: The key prop present on the removed <GrafanaRuleLoader> element was not carried over when the JSX was replaced with <GrafanaRuleListItem>.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-add key={key} to the <GrafanaRuleListItem ... /> element in the 'grafana' case, matching the key used for the other cases in the same map callback.
findings.title: Missing React key prop when rendering GrafanaRuleListItem in filtered rule list
findings.trigger: Rendering the 'grafana' branch of the switch inside rules.map() in FilterViewResults, which used to pass key={key} to GrafanaRuleLoader but now omits key on the replacement GrafanaRuleListItem element.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows GrafanaRuleLoader had key={key} at L158 but replacement GrafanaRuleListItem at R157-R162 omits key prop. Other branches (datasource at R165, default at R169) retain key={key}. Missing key in React list map causes reconciliation warnings and potential state issues.

raw_findings.body: React will emit a missing-key warning and may misidentify/re-mount list items on reordering or filtering, causing incorrect component state reuse (e.g. stale action menu state) across re-renders of the filtered rule list.
raw_findings.failure_mode: React list reconciliation degrades to index-based diffing for this branch, causing UI/console warnings and potential state bleed between list items.
raw_findings.impact: React will emit a missing-key warning and may misidentify/re-mount list items on reordering or filtering, causing incorrect component state reuse (e.g. stale action menu state) across re-renders of the filtered rule list.
raw_findings.root_cause: The key prop present on the removed <GrafanaRuleLoader> element was not carried over when the JSX was replaced with <GrafanaRuleListItem>.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Re-add key={key} to the <GrafanaRuleListItem ... /> element in the 'grafana' case, matching the key used for the other cases in the same map callback.
raw_findings.title: Missing React key prop when rendering GrafanaRuleListItem in filtered rule list
raw_findings.trigger: Rendering the 'grafana' branch of the switch inside rules.map() in FilterViewResults, which used to pass key={key} to GrafanaRuleLoader but now omits key on the replacement GrafanaRuleListItem element.

raw_findings.body: The rule detail view's 'back' / return-to-previous navigation no longer points to the originating list view, breaking the previous UX for users navigating from the alert list to a rule and back.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent loss of navigation context; no runtime error, only a UX regression on the 'view' link path.
raw_findings.impact: The rule detail view's 'back' / return-to-previous navigation no longer points to the originating list view, breaking the previous UX for users navigating from the alert list to a rule and back.
raw_findings.root_cause: The returnTo query-parameter construction logic was dropped when GrafanaRuleListItem was rewritten as a new component without porting over the useReturnTo/createReturnTo integration.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Reintroduce createReturnTo() and pass { returnTo } as the second argument to createRelativeUrl when building the view href, as was done in the previous GrafanaRuleListItem implementation.
raw_findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem no longer preserves 'returnTo' navigation state on the view link
raw_findings.trigger: Any user clicking a Grafana rule row link from the filtered/grouped rule list, which previously built the URL with a returnTo query parameter via createReturnTo() (in the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx GrafanaRuleListItem) so the rule detail page could navigate back to the list.

raw_findings.body: Type checking on promRule.provenance is unsound: the compiler either errors or silently treats the field as untyped, meaning non-Grafana PromRuleDTO variants passed to this function are not statically guaranteed to have a 'provenance' member, risking future refactors introducing a genuine undefined-access bug.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Loss of type safety around a newly introduced optional field, masking potential incorrect provenance checks for non-Grafana prom rules.
raw_findings.impact: Type checking on promRule.provenance is unsound: the compiler either errors or silently treats the field as untyped, meaning non-Grafana PromRuleDTO variants passed to this function are not statically guaranteed to have a 'provenance' member, risking future refactors introducing a genuine undefined-access bug.
raw_findings.root_cause: provenance was added only to GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase while isProvisionedPromRule was written against the broader, non-narrowed PromRuleDTO type.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Type the parameter as GrafanaPromRuleDTO (or make prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule a proper 'rule is GrafanaPromRuleDTO' type predicate) so provenance access is statically sound.
raw_findings.title: isProvisionedPromRule accesses .provenance on a type that does not guarantee it exists
raw_findings.trigger: Calling isProvisionedPromRule with a PromRuleDTO-typed value; prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule is a plain boolean-returning function (not a TypeScript type predicate), so it does not narrow promRule to a type that has 'provenance' — a field only added to GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase, not the shared PromRuleDTOBase.

raw_findings.body: The stray comment signals unresolved code duplication between useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable and useIsRuleEditable, making future maintenance confusing since it is unclear whether deduplication was intentionally deferred or accidentally left in.
raw_findings.evidence: const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reviewer/maintainer confusion about intended code duplication, increasing risk of divergent bug fixes applied to only one of the two near-identical hooks.
raw_findings.impact: The stray comment signals unresolved code duplication between useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable and useIsRuleEditable, making future maintenance confusing since it is unclear whether deduplication was intentionally deferred or accidentally left in.
raw_findings.root_cause: A development-time note was committed without cleanup or elaboration during the refactor introducing useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the stray '// duplicate' comment or replace it with a clear TODO explaining the plan to consolidate useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable with useIsRuleEditable.
raw_findings.title: Leftover 'duplicate' debug comment left in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities
raw_findings.trigger: Reading useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, which flags its own logic as '// duplicate' of useIsRuleEditable without any accompanying explanation, TODO ticket reference, or follow-up plan.

finding.verifier_reason: The code at L171-172 first calls prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) which returns true only for GrafanaPromRuleDTO types that have provenance. This is a speculative type-safety concern, not a concrete bug.
